genxml.title: AT&T/Lucent 11C1:5802 two-port OHCI USB host controller (Origin 300 IO-8), the register and identity facts the held sources establish
genxml.from: OpenHCI 1.0a (sections cited per item); Lucent USS-312 datasheet; Online Diagnostics manual 108-0286-007; IO-8 board test (io8bt) in the stock PROM diagnostics; public IRIX hinv capture of an Origin 300 IO-8
genxml.doc: The two-port USB host controller on the Origin 300 IO-8 board (PCI 11c1:5802, OpenHCI register interface). The register offsets follow the OpenHCI word layout; the IO-8 board test names its operational registers by word index. Grades say how each item was derived: established means the published OpenHCI specification, the Lucent USS-312 datasheet, a published SGI manual or a public hardware capture states it; inferred means a software expectation taken from the IO-8 board test's own checks, or a reading of its masks. No reset word for the PCI configuration Command and Status registers is held, and the reset values of the operational registers are unknown unless a row says otherwise. Software expectations are what the diagnostic requires, not measured chip behaviour.

struct.name: HC_INTERRUPT_ENABLE
struct.doc: Interrupt enable word. The IO-8 board test requires it to read zero after a host-controller reset issued through the command register, and it prints a reset-error message when it does not. That is the test's software expectation, not a value measured on the part. The test's mask table narrows the read-back masks of four fields: the unrecoverable-error enable in this word, the frame interval toggle, the frame remaining word and the top of the power-on-to-power-good time. Which bits of those the part keeps is unknown.

struct.name: HC_FM_INTERVAL
struct.doc: Frame interval word. The frame interval and its toggle take the OpenHCI reset values (see FRAME_INTERVAL_RESET). The largest data packet field's reset value is TBD in the OpenHCI specification, and the USS-312 data sheet gives it as 0h, which the IO-8 board test also expects.

struct.name: HC_FM_NUMBER
struct.from: OpenHCI 1.0a section 7.3.3 (printed page 122), as the source datasheet cites it; IO-8 board test register table for the write check (index 0xf, offset 0x3c)
struct.doc: Frame number word. The specification makes it read-only to the driver, written only by the controller, with reset zero. The IO-8 board test writes 0xffff to it after a controller reset, while the controller is not operational and again during reset, and requires the read-back to match under the mask in FM_NUMBER_WRITE_MASK. Neither the specification nor the test says what a driver write does to the part. That is the open point of this register.

struct.name: HC_RH_DESCRIPTOR_A
struct.doc: Root hub descriptor A. The specification makes the power-switching and over-current fields and the power-on-to-power-good time driver-written, so the board test's write-and-read-back of them is a fair check of those writable bits. The test writes zero and requires those fields to read back as zero under the mask 0x03001b00 (the bits of PowerSwitchingMode, NoPowerSwitching, OverCurrentProtectionMode and NoOverCurrentProtection, plus bits 25 and 24 of the power-on-to-power-good time). The power-on value is given by the USS-312 datasheet but is not stated in this unit.

struct.name: HC_RH_DESCRIPTOR_B
struct.doc: Root hub descriptor B. The specification gives the device-removable and port-power-control fields as driver written, one bit per port starting at bit 1 of each half, and says a hardware reset does not reset the root hub. The board test's USBRESET check requires the port bits to survive a USBRESET followed by a controller reset. The specification's prose points the other way about USBRESET, and its reset column permits keeping the fields, so the survival is inferred from the test alone.
